chapter: Riverboat to New Orleans and Horace Henderson
title: The Streckfuss excursion boats and riverboat work for musicians
summary: Boats of the St. Louis Streckfuss company saluted them; St. Louis musicians such as Red Allen played excursions, and Louisville had its own dance boats.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yes, you were saying that they all blew their whistles.

Yeah, saluting us, coming in. They do that, all the boats, and I guess they had about two or three boats with the Strekress (PHONETIC) Company, all the old guys had worked on, back in St. Louis, you know.
What was the first company you said?
Oh, yeah. Was it a shipping company?
Yeah, well Strekress Company, out of St. Louis.
That's who had a lot of boats, the pleasure boats, you know.
And a lot of the St. Louis musicians played on them, and Red Allen and all them guys played when they'd come up to -- left New Orleans, some of them would come up to St. Louis, you know.
Some from Chicago and some from St. Louis. A lot of them guys played on them boats out of -- excursions
running out of St. Louis, going up the river a piece and back, you know.

But they were doing that in a lot of places, because they did the same thing in Louisville. They'd play on them boats, and there were a couple of boats around Louisville there, they'd go up and back , you know, different clubs would give a dance or something like that.

Then sometimes they just have it open, anybody that's got a dollar, a dollar and a half, would -- could ride. And so that was quite a thing for them to salute us, and then the next thing that was great, what I enjoyed, is that this would be -- we'd be passing each other, because when you're in New Orleans you take this out every night, so the rest of the boats are going out too.
